$comment: The earcon vocabulary, the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for ids, meanings and maxMs. The set is three device pings (down from seven): the screen carries listening/thinking/answer/tool state, so most earcons were redundant with something already visible. Designed WAVs live in backend/assets/earcons/ (id.wav), loaded by backend/audio/speak.py via the stdlib wave module — no audio-codec dependency. maxMs is the ceiling the selfcheck holds each WAV under (a wrong/oversized file trips it). WHEN each fires, and WHETHER it plays at all (the 'Pings' toggle, default on), is the orchestrator's job.

earcons.meaning: a capture opened — wake word heard or ask-hotkey pressed. The audible 'I heard you'; the ONSET is latency-bounded (< 300 ms), the length is not (it rings out over the next phase)
a result landed well: a Tier-2 tool action completed, or a long answer is ready and shown on the Teleprompter. Later (unbuilt): a named timer fired
something needs your view: a tool action failed, the pipeline broke (model unreachable, STT failed, nothing transcribed), or a Tier-3 action is proposed and awaits your keypress / spoken 'confirm'
